## TL;DR


- Yes. Provision's[RFI Agent](https://provision.com/rfi-agent) reviews digital drawings and specifications against each other before tender closes.
- It surfaces more than 100 potential issues from a document set in an hour: conflicts, omissions, and unclear requirements.
- Every finding is source-traced to the exact specification page or drawing.
- An estimator reviews the findings, sets the action, and exports a single report to take to the owner and design team.
- RFI Agent does not auto-issue RFIs. It gives your team a reviewed shortlist to act on before bid day.


Short answer: yes. Provision's RFI Agent does exactly this. It reads the drawing set against the specifications, finds where they conflict, what they omit, and where requirements stay unclear, and returns a reviewed issue report in about an hour.


Longer answer: most pre-construction teams already know the problem. Conflicts buried in a 600-page drawing set do not surface until a sub asks a question on bid day, or until the problem lands in a change order after award. By then, your options are limited and expensive.


This article explains how construction drawing review software works in practice, what to look for when evaluating it, and how Provision's RFI Agent fits into the pre-tender workflow of a GC pre-construction team.


## Why Drawing Review Before Tender Matters


Pre-tender RFI management is one of the least systematic workflows in pre-construction. Most teams run a manual review: an estimator reads through drawings, flags obvious conflicts in a spreadsheet, and submits RFIs to the design team. The process depends on how experienced the estimator is and how much time the schedule allows.


Neither variable is reliable. Tender windows are compressing. Experienced estimators are stretched across multiple pursuits. And the volume of digital project documents keeps growing.


The result is predictable. Issues that could have been resolved before bid day become bid qualifications, change orders, or disputes after award. A 2024 Arcadis report put the average construction dispute value in North America at $60.1 million. "Errors and omissions in contract documents" ranks as a top dispute cause in North America. That is not a legal problem. It is a documentation problem that starts in pre-construction.


Automated construction drawing review software changes the math. It does not replace estimator judgment. It gives your estimator a prioritized list of issues to review in the time they actually have.


## What Does Software That Reviews Construction Drawings for RFI Issues Actually Do?


Provision's RFI Agent reviews digital drawings and specifications against each other for three categories of issues: conflicts, omissions, and unclear requirements. It processes the full document set together, not one file at a time. It surfaces more than 100 potential issues in an hour, with every finding tied to the exact drawing or specification page where the evidence appears.


The workflow has four steps.


1. **Upload the document set.** Drawings and specifications are uploaded as digital PDFs. RFI Agent reads both against each other.
2. **Review runs automatically.** The agent cross-references drawings and specs to identify conflicts, omissions, and unclear requirements across the full set.
3. **Estimator reviews the findings.** You filter by impact, conflict type, discipline, and review status. For each finding, you set the action: submit as an RFI, treat as a bid qualification, flag as a clarification, assign as a trade coordination item, log as a mitigation action, or take no action.
4. **Export the report.** The reviewed shortlist goes out as one report to the owner and design team before tender closes.


That is the whole workflow. The software does the discovery pass. The estimator makes every decision.


## What RFI Agent Does Not Do


This matters for teams evaluating any automated RFI generation tool for GCs.


RFI Agent does not automatically issue RFIs into your project management system. It does not confirm that every potential issue it surfaces is a material error. The counts it returns are potential issues raised for review, not confirmed defects.


The findings are starting points. They require estimator judgment. The tool surfaces more than your team would catch manually in the same window, and it does it faster. But it does not replace the person who understands the project.


This distinction matters because some teams have seen AI tools that issue outputs without review, then spend time defending or walking back those outputs in front of the owner and design team. RFI Agent does not do that. Everything goes through your estimator before anything leaves the building.


## How Is This Different From Reading the Documents Yourself?


Speed and coverage. A senior estimator doing a manual review of a 400-drawing set might catch 20 to 30 conflicts in a day, if the schedule allows a day. RFI Agent surfaces more than 100 potential issues in an hour, across the full document set, cross-referenced against specs.


Source tracing. Every finding in RFI Agent carries its source evidence: the exact specification page or drawing. You can verify any finding in seconds. You are not chasing a note in someone's spreadsheet.


Coverage consistency. A manual review is only as good as the estimator running it and the time they have. An automated review applies the same scrutiny to every drawing and every spec section, every time.


Markee Foster, a Project Manager at Clark Construction, described her team's experience this way after using RFI Agent on a live project:


> "I went through the first 30, and of the first 30 I picked close to 22 that I would have submitted as RFIs. It turned out that some of the subs we've been working with caught the same things."
>
>
> *Markee Foster, Project Manager, Clark Construction*


That is what good drawing review software looks like in practice. Not a list of everything. A list you can actually act on, with enough coverage that your subs are not finding things you missed.


## Where Drawing Conflicts Come From: Common Issue Types


Understanding what RFI Agent looks for helps clarify why manual review alone is not enough. Construction drawing sets are produced by multiple disciplines. Coordination between them is imperfect. Specific conflict types appear on nearly every project.


### Specification and Drawing Conflicts


A spec section calls for one material. The drawing calls for another. Neither is wrong in isolation. Together, they produce a scope question that a sub will eventually ask, usually at the worst time. Conflicts like the $45,000 stone-depth mismatch between civil, structural, and architectural drawings on a single slab are typical. They are findable before tender. They rarely get found.


### Omissions in the Drawing Set


Something is required by the design intent but not shown or specified anywhere. The $300,000 lead-lined glass omitted from a hospital imaging suite is a documented example. It was absorbed by the GC under "readily inferable" contract language. It was findable in the drawing set. It was not found before bid.


For more on how readily inferable language and scope omissions compound into change orders, see the[Scope Gap Playbook chapter on subcontract language](https://provision.com/ebooks/scope-gap-playbook/subcontract-language-scope) .


### Unclear Requirements


Drawings or specs that do not specify a requirement clearly enough for a sub to price it accurately. These produce scope interpretation risk: different subs price different things, and the GC carries the difference.


### MEP and Trade Coordination Issues


Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing drawings frequently conflict with each other and with structural drawings. Generator field conditioning, motor starters, fire-rated louvres, lighting controls: these are well-documented MEP scope gap categories. Conflicts between disciplines show up consistently on ICI projects. For a detailed breakdown by trade, see the[Scope Gap Playbook chapter on trade-specific scope gaps](https://provision.com/ebooks/scope-gap-playbook/trade-specific-scope-gaps) .

RFI Agent asks: "Where do the drawings conflict with themselves and with the specs, and what do I need to ask the owner?"


## What to Look for When Evaluating Construction Drawing Review Software


Not all tools in this category do the same thing. Here are the questions worth asking before you commit to any automated RFI generation tool.


### Does It Read Drawings, or Only Specs and Contracts?


Some document AI tools for construction read specs and contracts well. They do not read drawings. For pre-tender RFI work, drawing review is the core capability. A tool that only processes text documents will miss the conflicts that live in the drawing set.


### Does It Cross-Reference Drawings Against Specs?


Reading drawings alone is not enough. The most common and costly pre-tender issues come from conflicts between what the drawings show and what the specs require. The tool needs to process both together.


### Is Every Finding Source-Traced?


If a finding does not carry a citation to the exact page or drawing, your estimator cannot verify it efficiently. Source-tracing is not a nice-to-have. It is what makes the output usable in a pre-tender timeline.


### Does the Estimator Stay in Control?


Automated issue discovery is valuable. Automated issue issuance is a liability. Any tool you evaluate should give your team full control over which findings become RFIs, qualifications, or escalations. The software surfaces the issues. Your estimator decides what to do with each one.


### Can You Filter and Prioritize?


More than 100 potential issues is a lot to work through. The tool needs to let you filter by impact, discipline, and conflict type so your estimator works through the high-priority findings first. A flat list with no prioritization is not a workflow tool.


## The Business Case for Getting This Right Before Tender


The cost of a missed drawing conflict compounds at every stage. Before tender, it is an hour of review. After award, it is a change order. In a dispute, it is legal fees added to the original scope gap cost.


The $400,000 missed roof cover board on a $50 million project is a documented example from GC pre-construction practice. It was recovered only through a relational concession from the sub. That is not a risk management strategy. It is luck.


Pre-tender drawing review is where GCs with the best margins invest their time. Catching a conflict before tender costs one hour. Catching it after award costs multiples of that in time, money, and subcontractor goodwill. And failing to catch it at all costs the most.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is software that reviews construction drawings for RFI issues?


It is a tool that reads digital drawing sets and specifications against each other to find conflicts, omissions, and unclear requirements before tender closes. Provision's RFI Agent surfaces more than 100 potential issues in an hour, with every finding traced to the exact drawing or specification page. An estimator reviews the findings and decides which become RFIs, qualifications, or other actions.


### Does RFI Agent automatically submit RFIs to the owner or design team?


No. RFI Agent produces a reviewed issue report that your estimator acts on. Your team sets the action for each finding: submit as an RFI, flag as a bid qualification, treat as a clarification, or take no action. Nothing is issued automatically. The estimator controls every output before it leaves your team.


### How many issues can RFI Agent surface from a drawing set?


Provision's RFI Agent surfaces more than 100 potential issues from a document set in an hour. This is a throughput figure based on actual use. The count covers conflicts between drawings and specs, omissions, and unclear requirements across the full set. Not every finding will be material: your estimator reviews and filters the shortlist.


### What types of drawing conflicts does RFI Agent find?


RFI Agent identifies conflicts between drawings and specifications, omissions in the drawing set, unclear or underspecified requirements, and coordination issues across disciplines. Common examples include MEP coordination conflicts, material specification mismatches, and requirements that appear in one document but not another.


### How is RFI Agent different from Risk Review?


Risk Review answers the question: "What is my commercial exposure in this contract and spec set?" It reviews contracts, specs, and project documents for risk clauses, checklist items, and commercial conflicts. RFI Agent answers a different question: "Where do the drawings conflict with themselves and the specs, and what do I need to ask the owner?" They are separate tools for separate pre-construction workflows.


### Does construction drawing review software replace estimator judgment?


No. Software like RFI Agent runs the discovery pass: it finds more potential issues than a manual review in the same time window. The estimator still reviews every finding, sets the action, and decides what goes to the owner and design team. The tool handles coverage. The estimator handles judgment.


### What document formats does RFI Agent work with?


RFI Agent works with digital project documents, specifically digital PDFs of drawings and specifications. It is not designed for physical paper documents. The full document set is uploaded and reviewed together, so the cross-reference between drawings and specs covers the complete project, not individual files in isolation.
